2. Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and learned Addl. Standing Counsel for the State.
Perused the records.
3.

This is an application under Section 482, Cr.P.C. filed by the Petitioners for bail, involving offence punishable under Sections 409/420/468/471/294/506/120-B/34 of I.P.C. in G.R. Case No.93 of 2022 of the Court of learned J.M.F.C., (IV), Cog. Taking, Cuttack arising out of Chauliaganj P.S.
Case No-20 of 2022.
4. It is stated by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the father of the petitioner is the principal accused and against whom there is an allegation of taking money.
So far the present petitioner is concerned it is stated that against the son of the principal accused, there is no allegation of taking money.
He further contended that the petitioner is a student prosecuting his studies.

5. Learned counsel for the Petitioner during course of argument submits that the Petitioner does not want to press this application, but the Petitioner intends to surrender and move for bail before the court below, hence, he submit to direct the court below to dispose of the bail application of the Petitioner on the same day.

sentences.text: Considering the submission made, this CRLMC stands disposed of as not pressed.
7. Considering the nature of allegation, gravity of offence and the fact of the case, I am not inclined to grant bail to the Petitioner.

However, it is directed that in the event the Petitioner surrenders before the Court in seisin over the matter within a period of four weeks from today and move an application for bail, the Court in seisin over the matter shall release him on bail in connection with the aforesaid case on such terms and conditions as it may deem just and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.
8. The CRLMC is disposed of accordingly.
9. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted as per rules.
( A.K. Mohapatra) Judge Rubi Location: High Court of Orissa, Cuttack Laxmikant Sahoo vs State Of Odisha .....
